paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi leh Aaron ahoupih a,
heading: Vun Natna Toh Kisai Dante
english: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

paite: "Mi vun a, akhem hiam, abol hiam, phak hileh kilawm akimuhleh siampu Aaron kiang ah hiam, atapa siampute lak a kua pen hiam kiang api ding ahi.
english: “When a man shall have a rising in his body’s skin, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body the plague of leprosy, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons, the priests:

paite: Siampu in avun a hii pen ana en dia, ahii omna amul akan a, ahii pen avun sang a thukzaw a akimuhleh phak ahi a, siampu in amah ana en dia, misiang lou in apuang ding ahi.
english: and the priest shall examine the plague in the skin of the body: and if the hair in the plague has turned white, and the appearance of the plague is deeper than the body’s skin, it is the plague of leprosy; and the priest shall examine him, and pronounce him unclean.

paite: Avun a bolte akan a, avun sang a thukzaw a akimuh keileh, amul akan keileh hii nei mi pen siampu in ni sagih sung akhumtuam ding hi.
english: If the bright spot is white in the skin of his body, and its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, and its hair hasn’t turned white, then the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.

paite: Siampu in ani sagih ni in amah a-en dia; ngai dih, ahii pen angeingei a amuh a, ahii pen avun a azamzak keileh siampu in ni sagih mah akhumtuam nawn ding hi.
english: The priest shall examine him on the seventh day, and, behold, if in his eyes the plague is arrested, and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall isolate him for seven more days.

paite: Siampu in ni sagih ni in a-en nawn dia; ngai dih, hii pen amial a, hii pen avun a azamzak keileh siampu in asiang chih apuang ding ahi. Akhem lel ahi a, apuante asawp dia, ahong siang ding hi.
english: The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day; and behold, if the plague has faded, and the plague hasn’t spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. It is a scab. He shall wash his clothes, and be clean.

paite: Himahleh asiansakna ding a siampu aki-etsak nung a akhem pen avun a azamzak luatleh siampu aki-ensak nawn ding ahi:
english: But if the scab spreads on the skin, after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall show himself to the priest again.

paite: Siampu in a-en dia, ngai in, akhem pen avun a azamzakleh siampu in siang lou chih apuang dia, hiai phak ahi.
english: The priest shall examine him; and behold, if the scab has spread on the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy.

paite: "Mi'n phak hii avomleh siampu kiang a pi ding ahi;
english: “When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought to the priest;

paite: Siampu in ana en dia, ngai dih, avun a akang a-om khiak a, amul akansak a, abawk dulh hethutleh,
english: and the priest shall examine him. Behold, if there is a white rising in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the rising,

paite: asa a phak kumlui om ahi a, siampu in siang lou ahi chih apuang dia, himahleh amah siang lou ahih ziak a khumtuam ding ahi kei hi.
english: it is a chronic leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He shall not isolate him, for he is unclean.

paite: Aphak pen avun a azamzak mahmah a, ahii veimi vun, alu a pan akhe tan a siampu theih chiang phak in abopleh, siampu'n a-en ding hi.
english: “If the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the infected person from his head even to his feet, as far as it appears to the priest;

paite: Ngai dih, phak in asa tengteng abop suaksa ahihleh, hii veimi asiang chih apuang dia, akang khinta a, asiangta hi.
english: then the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean of the plague. It has all turned white: he is clean.

paite: Himahleh asa adulh hethutleh, siang lou ahi dia,
english: But whenever raw flesh appears in him, he shall be unclean.

paite: Siampu in asa dulh hethut a-en dia, siang lou in apuang ding hi. Sa dulh hethut pen siang lou ahi a, phak ahi.
english: The priest shall examine the raw flesh, and pronounce him unclean: the raw flesh is unclean. It is leprosy.

paite: Himahleh sa dulh hethut pen ana lamdan nawn a, ana kan nawnleh siampu kiang ah ahoh ding hi.
english: Or if the raw flesh turns again, and is changed to white, then he shall come to the priest;

paite: Siampu in ana en dia; ngai dih, ahii akanleh siampu in hii veimi asiang lou kei chih apuang ding hi. Amah asiangta hi.
english: and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the plague has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him clean of the plague. He is clean.

paite: "Asa leh avun a om meimatum ahi a, adamta hi.
english: “When the body has a boil on its skin, and it has healed,

paite: Ameimatum omna mun ana kan a na san hiam, kang san deuh a na bol hiam ahihleh, siampu in a-et ding ahi.
english: and in the place of the boil there is a white rising, or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be shown to the priest;

paite: Siampu in ana en dia, ngai dih, avun sang a thukzaw a akimuh a, amul akanleh siampu in siang lou in apuang ding ahi: phak hii ahi a, meimatum hong suakkhia ahi.
english: and the priest shall examine it; and behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy. It has broken out in the boil.

paite: Himahleh siampu in ana et a, ngai dih, mul kang a-om louh a, amial sim phet ahihleh, siampu in ni sagih akhumtuam ding a:
english: But if the priest examines it, and behold, there are no white hairs in it, and it isn’t deeper than the skin, but is dim, then the priest shall isolate him seven days.

paite: Avun a azamzakleh siampu in siang lou in apuang ding hi.
english: If it spreads in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a plague.

paite: Himahleh abol ngou pen a-omna ngei a om a, azamzak keileh meimatum pawn lel ahi a; siampu in asiangthou chih apuang ding ahi.
english: But if the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread, it is the scar from the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.

paite: "Ahihkeileh avun polna mun asa a-om a, akang hiam, asan sim hiam ahihkeileh angouleh,
english: “Or when the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white, or white,

paite: siampu in ana en dia, ngai dih, apolna laitak a mul pen akan a, huchi avun sang a thukzaw a akimuhleh phak ahi a, meikat ahong omkhia phak ahi a, siampu in siang lou in apuang ding ahi, hiai phak hii ahi.
english: then the priest shall examine it; and behold, if the hair in the bright spot has turned white, and its appearance is deeper than the skin; it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.

paite: Himahleh siampu in ana et a, ngai dih, apol a mul kang om lou a, avun sang a thuk lou zaw a, mial deuh lel ahihleh siampu in ni sagih akhumtuam ding ahi.
english: But if the priest examines it, and behold, there is no white hair in the bright spot, and it isn’t lower than the skin, but is faded; then the priest shall isolate him seven days.

paite: Siampu in ni sagih ni in amah a-en dia, avun a azamzak luatleh siampu in asiang lou in apuang ding hi, hiai phak hii ahi.
english: The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.

paite: Apol pen a-omna ngei a ana omdet a, vun a azamzak keileh, mial deuh lel ahihleh meikat bawk lel ahi a, siampu in asiang chih apuang ding ahi; meikang pawn lel ahi.
english: If the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread in the skin, but is faded, it is the swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean; for it is the scar from the burn.

paite: "Numei hiam, pasal hiam in alu ah hiam, akhamul lak ah hiam hii aveileh
english: “When a man or woman has a plague on the head or on the beard,

paite: Siampu in hii pen ana en dia; ngai dih, avun sang a thukzaw a akimuh a, amul eng ngattak a-omleh siampu in siang lou in apuang ding ahi; meima sungtum ahi a, alu hiam akhamul hiam phak ahi.
english: then the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and the hair in it is yellow and thin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is an itch, it is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

paite: Siampu in meima sungtum hii pen a-et a, ngai dih, avun sang a thuk lou zaw a akimuh a, amul vom a-om keileh siampu in meima sungtum hii veimi pen ni sagih akhumtuam ding hi.
english: If the priest examines the plague of itching, and behold, its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest shall isolate him the person infected with itching seven days.

paite: Ni sagih ni in siampu in hii a-en dia, ngai dih, meima sungtum azamzak louh a, mul eng a-om keileh, meima sungtum a vun sang a thukzaw a akimuh keileh,
english: On the seventh day the priest shall examine the plague; and behold, if the itch hasn’t spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the appearance of the itch isn’t deeper than the skin,

paite: met ding ahi a, meima sungtum laitak bel amet ding ahi kei; siampu in meima sungtum neimi ni sagih dang akhumtuam nawn ding ahi.
english: then he shall be shaved, but he shall not shave the itch; and the priest shall shut him up who has the itch seven more days.

paite: Ni sagih ni in siampu in meima sungtum a-en nawn dia; ngai dih, meima sungtum pen avun a azak louh a, avun sang a thukzaw a akimuh keileh, siampu in siang in apuang ding ahi. Huchi in apuante asawp dia, ahong siangta ding hi.
english: On the seventh day, the priest shall examine the itch; and behold, if the itch hasn’t spread in the skin, and its appearance isn’t deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. He shall wash his clothes, and be clean.

paite: Himahleh meima sungtum pen akisiansak nung a, avun a azamzak luatleh,
english: But if the itch spreads in the skin after his cleansing,

paite: siampu in amah ana en dia, ngai dih, meima sungtum pen avun a, azamzakleh, siampu a ding in mul eng zon akiphamoh chitchiat kei ding; amah siang lou ahi.
english: then the priest shall examine him; and behold, if the itch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not look for the yellow hair; he is unclean.

paite: Himahleh meima sungtum pen angeingei a amuh a, mul vom apouleh, meima sungtum adamta ahi a, amah a siang a, siampu in asiang, chih apuang ding hi.
english: But if in his eyes the itch is arrested, and black hair has grown in it; the itch is healed, he is clean. The priest shall pronounce him clean.

paite: "Numei hiam, pasal hiam, avun ah pol, pol ngou kilhkelh ana omleh,
english: “When a man or a woman has bright spots in the skin of the body, even white bright spots;

paite: siampu in a-en dia, ngai dih, avun a pol pen mialngou sim lel ahihleh pol lel ahi a, vun a hong suak ahi a, amah asiang hi.
english: then the priest shall examine them; and behold, if the bright spots on the skin of their body are a dull white, it is a harmless rash, it has broken out in the skin; he is clean.

paite: Asam pulhsiang mi lugiau ahi; himahleh amah asiang hi.
english: “If a man’s hair has fallen from his head, he is bald. He is clean.

paite: Asip sam apulh siangleh talkolh ahi a, himahleh amah asiang hi.
english: If his hair has fallen off from the front part of his head, he is forehead bald. He is clean.

paite: Himahleh lugiau hiam, talkolh hiam ah, hii san sim a ngou a-omleh, alugiau hiam, atalkolh hiam phak ahi.
english: But if there is in the bald head, or the bald forehead, a reddish-white plague; it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head, or his bald forehead.

paite: Huchi in siampu in ana en dia, ngai dih, alugiau hiam, atalkolh hiam a hii hong bawkkhia pen asan simleh ngou sim hethut a, avun a phak bang akimuhleh,
english: Then the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the rising of the plague is reddish-white in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh,

paite: amah phak ahi a, siang lou ahi. Siampu in siang lou a apuan ngeingei ding ahi, alu ah phakna a-om hi.
english: he is a leprous man. He is unclean. The priest shall surely pronounce him unclean. His plague is on his head.

paite: "Phak hii veimi puante bohkek ahi dia, asamte khah ahi dia, amuk tunglam atuam dia, siang lou, siang lou, chi in akikou ding ahi.
english: “The leper in whom the plague is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his head shall hang loose. He shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’

paite: Phak in abop sung teng siang lou ahi dia; siang lou ahi a, atengtuam dia; giahphual pua ah ateng ding hi.
english: All the days in which the plague is in him he shall be unclean. He is unclean. He shall dwell alone. Outside of the camp shall be his dwelling.

paite: "Phak hii omna puansilh, samul puan hiam, khauzang ngat puan hiam;
heading: Phak Hii Kaina Toh Kisai
english: “The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, whether it is a woolen garment, or a linen garment;

paite: agatthoh hiam, aphanthoh hiam; khauzang ngat hiam, samul hiam, savun hiam, bangpeuh savun a bawl ah hiam; savun hiam, bangpeuh savun a bawl ah hiam, savun hiam,
english: whether it is in warp, or woof; of linen, or of wool; whether in a skin, or in anything made of skin;

paite: gat ah hiam, phan ah hiam, bangpeuh savun a bawl ah hiam ahing sim hiam a adawkkhiakleh, phak hii ahi a, siampu in a-en ding hi.
english: if the plague is greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything made of skin; it is the plague of leprosy, and shall be shown to the priest.

paite: Siampu in hii a-en dia, hii omna ni sagih akhumtuam ding hi.
english: The priest shall examine the plague, and isolate the plague seven days.

paite: Ni sagih ni in hii a-en dia, hii pen puansilh, gat ah hiam, phan ah hiam, savun ah hiam, bang ding peuh a leng azat uh savunte ah hiam, azamleh hii pen phakkip mahmah chi ahihleh siang lou ahi.
english: He shall examine the plague on the seventh day. If the plague has spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in the skin, whatever use the skin is used for, the plague is a destructive mildew. It is unclean.

paite: Puansilh, gatthoh hiam, phanthoh hiam, samul hiam, khauzang ngat hiam, savun a bawl chi himhim hiam, phak omna peuhmah hal ding ahi; phakkip mahmah chi ahi ngal a, hal ngeingei ding ahi.
english: He shall burn the garment, whether the warp or the woof, in wool or in linen, or anything of skin, in which the plague is: for it is a destructive mildew. It shall be burned in the fire.

paite: "Siampu in ana et a, huchi a, ngai dih, puansilh, gat hiam, phan hiam, savun a bawl chi himhim ah leng hii pen azam keileh
english: “If the priest examines it, and behold, the plague hasn’t spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin;

paite: hii omna siampu in sawp ding thu ape dia, ni sagih dang akhumtuam nawn ding hi.
english: then the priest shall command that they wash the thing in which the plague is, and he shall isolate it seven more days.

paite: Hii omna sawp ahih khit nung in siampu in ana en nawn dia, ngai dih, huai hii latdan akikhek keileh hii pen zam kei mahleh, asiang tuan kei, mei a na hal ding ahi; akipchi ahi, asunglam hiam, apolam hiam agiauleh leng.
english: Then the priest shall examine it, after the plague is washed; and behold, if the plague hasn’t changed its color, and the plague hasn’t spread, it is unclean; you shall burn it in the fire. It is a mildewed spot, whether the bareness is inside or outside.

paite: Siampu in ana et a, huchi a, ngai dih, sawp khit nung a mial sim lel ahihleh puansilh a pan hiam, savun a pan hiam, gat a pan hiam, phan a pan hiam abotkhe ding ahi.
english: If the priest looks, and behold, the plague has faded after it is washed, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof:

paite: Puansilh pen, gat ah hiam, phan ah hiam, savun bawl ah hiam alat lailai leh ahong pawt nawn ahi a; hii omna pen na hal ding ahi.
english: and if it appears again in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin, it is spreading. You shall burn with fire that in which the plague is.

paite: Puansilh, gat hiam, phan hiam, bangpeuh savun a bawl chi himhim hiam na sawp a, hii in anutsiatleh sawp nawn ding ahi a, huchi in ahong siangta ding hi.
english: The garment, either the warp, or the woof, or whatever thing of skin it is, which you shall wash, if the plague has departed from them, then it shall be washed the second time, and it will be clean.”

paite: "Hiai bel, puansilh samul hiam, khauzang ngat hiam, gat hiam, phan hiam, savun a bawl chi himhim hiam a phak hii om asian leh sian louh puanna dan ding ahi," chi in.
english: This is the law of the plague of mildew in a garment of wool or linen, either in the warp, or the woof, or in anything of skin, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.
